examples.question_text:
The table gives pipe capacities in kL/h. A dash means no connection.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{From / To}&A&B&C&D\\\hline A&-&-&-&-\\B&9&-&-&-\\C&-&7&-&11\\D&8&-&-&-\end{array}$
Identify the source and sink, then draw the weighted directed flow network.

examples.solution_text:
Record each edge in the row of the vertex it leaves and the column of the vertex it enters.
Row $P$ records $P\to Q$ and $P\to T$. Row $Q$ records $Q\to T$. Row $R$ records $R\to P$ and $R\to Q$. No edge leaves $T$.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{From / To}&P&Q&R&T\\\hline P&-&5&-&10\\Q&-&-&-&14\\R&16&12&-&-\\T&-&-&-&-\end{array}$
The source $R$ is drawn on the right; arrow directions determine the entries, regardless of vertex position. Capacities remain in tonnes per hour.

methods.description: Identify source and sink, then convert each connection entry into an edge directed from its row vertex to its column vertex and labelled with its capacity. Context, vertex count and heading order are variants of this method.

coverage.summary: Added three worked examples covering all distinct assessed methods with changed values and separate editable prompts and solutions. Diagrams use black ink and mid-line arrows; solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. No relation-led calculations require phantom gutters. Practice and quiz content were used only for method classification. Final-size diagram and label verification remains for the capture stage.

examples.derivation: Reading the table independently gives B→A with capacity 9, C→B with capacity 7, C→D with capacity 11 and D→A with capacity 8. Column C has no incoming connection and row A has no outgoing connection, establishing source C and sink A. The solution diagram contains exactly these four directed edges and capacities. This adapts the supplied table-to-directed-network exercise and flow-network definitions.

Following the authored arrows independently gives R→P=16, R→Q=12, P→Q=5, P→T=10 and Q→T=14. In heading order P,Q,R,T, the rows are P: [dash,5,dash,10], Q: [dash,dash,dash,14], R: [16,12,dash,dash] and T: [dash,dash,dash,dash]. These match the solution table. Source R remains identifiable by arrow direction despite its position on the right. The method matches the supplied directed graph-to-table examples.

The table requires S→A=18, S→B=13, A→B=6, A→T=15 and B→T=17. The prompt diagram supplies the two edges leaving S and the edge leaving B. Therefore the missing edges are exactly A→B with capacity 6 and A→T with capacity 15. The solution diagram preserves all givens and adds both required edges with correct arrow directions and labels. This follows the supplied partial-network completion exercise.

review.summary: All three distinct assessed methods are covered, and all 24 exact assessment locators are mapped appropriately. There are no existing examples to audit and no syllabus exception is required. Each example separates prompt and solution, uses supported single-dollar mathematics, preserves editable prose and uses black planar diagrams with mid-line arrows. No continuation gutters are needed. Solution prose and mathematics inherit the supplied renderer styling. Final-size label and layout verification remains for the capture stage; practice and quiz mathematics were not re-audited.
